why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 only tests that padLeft is exported, pads on the left with fill, uses a space when fill is left out, and gives results exactly width long. Check 2 only tests that s comes back unchanged when it is width long or longer, including width 0. Check 3 requires a README heading that names each exported function, with text describing it. That is what "a section for" a function means. Check 4 requires exit code 0 and `fail 0`. This is borderline as exact wording, but under `node --test` exit 0 and no failing tests mean the same thing, so it adds nothing beyond "passes". The stricter items (checking that test/strutil.test.js has padLeft tests, and multi-character fill or non-string s) are listed under "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)". No mutation tests, branch rules or file-scope rules appear in any PASS or FAIL condition.
